clue.text: Remarkable men help on a redevelopment

indicators.note: a redevelopment rebuilds something in a new form, so these four words are rebuilt into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some men help out on a building redevelopment that turns out impressively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redevelopment' looks like the subject of the sentence but signals the anagram of MEN HELP ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phenomenal is extraordinary, a synonym of remarkable.

clue.text: Exercises absorbing very large model

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A workout regime that takes in a very big fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To model is to pose for an artist or photographer.

clue.text: It's odd a vile note can be uplifting

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put into an irregular order

explanation.surface: It is strange that a nasty letter could raise someone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'can be' are links; 'odd' signals rearranging A VILE NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a raising up, which is what uplifting means as a noun.

clue.text: None over ten look at this flower

indicators.note: over means the letter for none is placed above the next in this down clue

parts.note: O is zero, none
X is the Roman numeral ten
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Not one of ten people would look at this bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a common wild bloom with a yellow centre.

clue.text: Create an impression

parts.note: read literally: to cut a design into a surface, making a physical impression rather than a social one

explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut lines into metal or wood, literally impressing a design.

clue.text: May appear alert, with craft or without craft

indicators.note: may appear suggests the word shows up in a different guise, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: Someone may look alert, whether skilled or unskilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May appear' is the anagram signal working on 'alert'; 'craft' is used twice by the setter, once as a ship and once in the definition meaning skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means naive and guileless, lacking cunning or skill.

clue.text: He's put soldiers back in charge

indicators.note: back tells us the word for soldiers is written right to left

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A man puts the troops back under command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the soldiers round. RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps; the 's of 'He's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a common boy's name, so its bearer is a male person, a he.

clue.text: Some upstaged tragedians felt really angry

indicators.note: some means part of the word, so the answer is found inside it

explanation.surface: Upstaged actors in tragic roles were furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstaged' is a link in the surface; 'Some' signals the letters within 'tragedians'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raged means fumed with fury, felt intense anger.

clue.text: Reading about medicine turn-over being critical

indicators.note: about puts the reading word around the medicine piece

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or reading

indicators.note: turn-over means the medicine abbreviation is flipped round

explanation.surface: Reading about a drug turnover with a critical eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-over' flips the medicine abbreviation, and 'about' wraps the reading word round it. To con is an old verb for studying a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemning means censuring severely, expressing strong disapproval.

clue.text: Cheats music men?

explanation.surface: Swindling musicians?
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to swindle, and a fiddle is a violin, so the word covers both swindlers and violinists.

clue.text: Cattle fodder from Northern Europe

definitions.meaning: a root vegetable, the yellow turnip, grown to feed livestock
a native of ..., a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: Winter feed for livestock imported from Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: The swede is a turnip-like root fed to cattle, and a Swede is a person from Sweden.

clue.text: Making some progress, though plainly ageing

definitions.meaning: advancing or doing well in a task

explanation.surface: Advancing steadily, even if obviously growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both advancing in a task and growing old in years, two idiomatic senses.

clue.text: Going in left and right one scoffed to wound

indicators.note: going in says one piece is placed inside the pair made from left and right

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: Someone bolts their food, left and right, ready to inflict injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going in' places the card between the left and right letters; 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear the flesh, a way to injure badly.

clue.text: Key in important Venetian scheme

indicators.note: in tells us the key's letter is placed within the Venetian ruler's title

parts.note: the Doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A key element in a plan by a prominent citizen of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or ruse, much like a scheme.

clue.text: Bet at cards-tricky if inattentive

indicators.note: tricky suggests something devious, so the letters are worked into a cunning new order

explanation.surface: A wager at cards is risky if you are not paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' signals rearranging BET AT CARDS; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstracted means lost in thought, absent-minded.

clue.text: Ordered to carry equipment for a military body

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: Soldiers commanded to transport their kit for the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like the command but gives BADE, which holds RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a large army unit made up of several battalions.

clue.text: They'll put on speculators

definitions.meaning: people who don a garment or adopt a manner
people who take things for granted or suppose

explanation.surface: People who will dress up as gamblers.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to don or adopt, and also to suppose, so the noun covers both those who don and those who suppose.

clue.text: Advances a member of the family

definitions.meaning: moves forward, read as two words: treads forward
a relative by marriage, a spouse's male child

explanation.surface: A relative makes progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means moves forward; as one it is a husband's or wife's male child from an earlier union.

clue.text: A monocle that's just for show

definitions.meaning: a single eyeglass, half a pair of glasses

explanation.surface: A single eyeglass worn purely for effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass is jokingly one of a pair of glasses, and the word also means an impressive display.

clue.text: A suit in material right for a hot country

indicators.note: material is taken as cloth to be cut and remade, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A suit made of fabric suitable for a warm country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like the fabric of the suit but signals rearranging A SUIT IN; 'right for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African nation with a famously warm climate.

clue.text: Rather slow before-and at the top!

indicators.note: at the top places the second word above the first in this down entry

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: Fairly sluggish beforehand, and at the summit too!
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Getting money back on a horse

parts.note: P stands for penny, a coin of money
astern means towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Winning cash back on a racehorse bet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests betting; really 'on a horse' is the definition, a part found on a horse. 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is the part of a horse's leg between fetlock and hoof.

clue.text: Professional examination giving rise to complaint

parts.note: a pro is a professional
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A professional exam sparks grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is an objection or expression of grievance.

clue.text: Warning a trainee to prepare for action

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to arm is to make ready for battle

explanation.surface: Telling a recruit to get ready for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal of danger, a kind of alert.

clue.text: Tired of everything trendy

parts.note: all means everything
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Weary of all things fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal for exhausted.

clue.text: Taking up rods to switch non-conformists

indicators.note: to switch is to change round, so the letters are swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: Picking up fishing rods to change over, like rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' is a link; 'switch' signals rearranging UP RODS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropouts are people who reject conventional society, so rebels who refuse to fit in.

clue.text: A cat that weighs very little?

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard of Central Asia
a small unit of weight, about 28 grams

explanation.surface: A very light cat?
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is another name for the snow leopard and also a tiny weight unit.

clue.text: Reports from every direction

definitions.meaning: the four compass points north, east, west and south

explanation.surface: Dispatches arriving from all over.
explanation.definitionFit: News means fresh information, and its letters are the initials of the four compass points.

clue.text: Day-dreaming about Spanish urging patience

indicators.note: about puts one piece around the other

parts.note: a trance is a dazed, dreamy state
ole is the Spanish cry of encouragement at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A dreamy spectator at a bullfight, Spanish cheers ringing out, waits calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is forbearance, the capacity to put up with things calmly.

clue.text: In a panic held off recess

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In a frenzy, someone avoids taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters run across 'panic held'; 'a' and 'off' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is an alcove set into a wall, a small recess.

clue.text: Daughter-one of 23

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter is one of a group of twenty-three.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' points to the answer at 23 down, ALL IN, meaning tired, so the definition is 'of 23', exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the sense of worn out is a synonym of exhausted, the sense of 23 down.

clue.text: Indulgence in grub by the head

parts.note: a gentle is an angler's name for a maggot used as bait
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Overindulging in food under the headmaster's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTLE (a maggot) is an anglers' word; NESS is a promontory. 'in' and 'by the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentleness is mildness and leniency, a kind of tolerant indulgence.
